amendments.rule: **A subordinating conjunction the ASV supplies for a clause whose Hebrew writes none is `added`.** Casuistic law opens its protasis with אִם, with כִּי, or with a waw, and where one of these stands in the clause it takes the ASV's *if*, *when* or *that* by rules 14 and 30: the corpus aligns a waw to *if* and to *when*, and כִּי takes whichever of them the ASV has written for it. But the ASV also writes such a word for a clause that has no conjunction in it at all — *and, behold,* ***if*** *the plague be spread* for וְהִנֵּה פָּשָׂה הַנֶּגַע, and the italic ***yet*** of *he is bald,* ***yet*** *is he clean* for קֵרֵחַ הוּא טָהוֹר הוּא — and there no morpheme licenses it: it is its own `added` unit under rule 30. Do not fold it into the waw that opens the clause, into הִנֵּה, or into the verb, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and* and rule 51 about a supplied *also* — the word is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them, and the waw and הִנֵּה already have the *and* and the *behold* the ASV wrote for them. Count the clause's conjunctions against the ASV's subordinators, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s, and mark whichever side is in surplus. **But a coordinator and a subordinator the ASV writes together for one waw are one rendering of that waw, and neither word is a surplus.** Where the ASV recasts a waw's own clause as a subordinate one and writes the pair at that clause's left edge — *And when I looked* for וָאֶרְאֶה, *And when I see the blood* for וְרָאִיתִי, and likewise *and that* and *so that* — both English words belong to the waw's single unit, and the count above marks nothing `added` unless no conjunction stands in the clause at all. Contiguity is the test, exactly as in rule 30: what makes the Leviticus *if* above a surplus is that הִנֵּה's *behold* stands between it and the waw's *and*, so the *if* is written beside those renderings rather than as part of one connective. Head such a unit on the coordinator, which is what the waw itself is; the corpus aligns a waw to *and when* in twenty-seven units, to *so that* in thirty-eight and to *and that* in eight, heading eleven of the *and when* units on *when* instead, so name that competing reading in the note under rule 8. An ASV italic on such a word corroborates it, and the absence of one is not evidence against it, by rule 7. **And a word that belongs to a formula's own fixed English rendering is not a subordinator supplied for the clause: it belongs to the morpheme the formula rests on.** The oath חַי־אָנִי is written *As I live*, and the *As* is what English spends on the adverbial force of that predicate adjective, exactly as rule 20 takes the copula from the construction and rule 30 takes the pronouns of נָא's *I beseech thee* from the particle's one idiomatic rendering: the adjective takes *As … live* in one unit, discontinuous around the pronoun under rule 25 and headed on *live*, while an explicit אָנִי or אֲנִי takes only its own *I*. The corpus reads the formula this way in six chapters and never marks the *As* `added`. So before counting an English subordinator as a surplus, read whether it is one the formula always writes; the count above governs a word the ASV has supplied for the clause, not a word the formula's rendering contains.
amendments.why: This chapter's verse pass read rule 55's opening sentence onto the oath formula חַי־אָנִי and marked the 'As' of 'As I live' added, because the Hebrew clause writes no conjunction. The requested corpus round contradicts that: חַי before a 1cs pronoun is aligned to 'as live', headed on 'live', in six chapters — DEU.32.40, EZK.16.48, EZK.20.3, EZK.20.31 and two more — with notes saying the adverbial predicate licenses the supplied 'As', and the eighteen units for the following pronoun give it 'I' alone. Left as it stood, rule 55's over-broad first sentence would keep producing that error in every oath formula a later chapter meets, and a new rule pointing back at it would leave the sentence in place for whoever reads it first. The qualification is written into rule 55 itself and cites rules 20, 25 and 30, which are what actually place the word.

conventions: Oath formula חַי־אָנִי: the ASV writes 'As I live', and the supplied 'As' belongs to the predicate adjective חַי, whose unit is the discontinuous 'As ... live' headed on 'live'; the explicit pronoun אָנִי takes only 'I'. The corpus reads it this way in six chapters, EZK.16.48, EZK.20.3 and EZK.20.31 among them. Treating the 'As' as a subordinator supplied for a conjunctionless clause, and so 'added' under rule 55, was tried in this chapter's verse pass and reversed at reconciliation.

אִם־לֹא introducing an oath's content and rendered by the single word 'surely' is 'noncompositional', source head on אִם as the deterministic anchor and target head on 'surely': the polarity reversal leaves neither morpheme's own sense in the English. Compositional fusions keep 'aligned' status — לָכֵן → 'Therefore'/'Wherefore', מִשָּׁם → 'thereof', מִמֶּנּוּ → 'therefrom' — because each morpheme's sense survives in the one English word. Read which kind of fusion is in hand before choosing the status.

אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה is rendered 'the Lord Jehovah': the supplied 'the' goes with אֲדֹנָי as the nominal expression it determines (rule 15), and the word's 1cs suffix is 'unrepresented', the ASV writing no possessive for it (5.5, 5.7, 5.8, 5.11). All four Sp1cs disagreements BSB reports on this chapter are this one decision.

סְבִיבוֹת plus its suffix is one English rendering 'round about', headed on 'round' as the lexeme-carrying word. Where the phrase is the predicate of a verbless clause the construction-supplied copula joins it — 'countries are round about her', 'that are round about you' (5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.14, 5.15) — and where it is adverbial to a written verb no copula is written and none is placed (5.2, 5.12). The suffix keeps its own pronoun in every case.

report: Read all 37 candidate lemma groups end to end. Every printed difference is the ASV writing a different English word in a different context, and the source licenses each: the waw's then/so/thus/moreover/therefore against its many 'and's (5.1, 5.11, 5.13-5.15); בְּ as in/with/by/upon/through/among; the articles that go unrepresented exactly where the ASV writes 'a third part' or 'with famine'; and the object markers that take 'against' only in 5.6, where the ASV spends a preposition on 'rebelled against', and go bare in 5.7 and 5.16, where it does not. No cross-verse split in the table.

The table is blind to added units, so I read all ten from the dump. They are internally consistent: supplied object pronouns with no object morpheme are added in 5.1 (it), 5.11 (thee), 5.15 and 5.17 (it); supplied connectives with no waw in the clause are added in 5.2 and 5.7; 5.6's 'doing' and 'as for' fall under the explicit limits in rules 20 and 16. The one inconsistency is with the corpus rather than within the chapter, and it is in 5.11.

EZK.5.11, correction 1: the 'as' of 'As I live' is no longer added. The requested corpus round is decisive — חַי before a 1cs pronoun aligns to 'as live', headed on 'live', in six chapters including EZK.16.48, EZK.20.3 and EZK.20.31, and אֲנִי after it takes only 'I' in all eighteen units. The verse pass reached the added by applying rule 55's opening sentence to a formula that rule had not considered; the amendment below closes that.

EZK.5.11, correction 2: אִם־לֹא → 'surely' becomes noncompositional (same arrays, same heads, status only). The corpus reads the two-token phrase that way in six of seven occurrences, the seventh (1KI.20.25) conceding it in its own note. The polarity reversal leaves neither morpheme's sense in the English word, which is rule 6's criterion; this chapter's compositional fusions — לָכֵן, מִשָּׁם, מִמֶּנּוּ — stay aligned under rule 30.

BSB: no genuine error among the disagreements. The six R and six Td tokens are the documented convention difference — BSB attaches a recast preposition to its phrase and an article to its word, while rules 40 and 29/47 leave them unrepresented where the ASV writes nothing (5.1 'take thee', 5.6 'rejected mine ordinances', 5.14 'make thee a desolation', 5.16 'break your staff'; 'a barber's razor', 'a third part' ×3, 'with famine', and the agreement article of 5.16). The three אוֹתָם markers (5.3, 5.4 ×2) are rule 16's majority ruling. The four Sp1cs are the suffix of אֲדֹנָי, for which the ASV writes no possessive. The one substantive candidate is 5.9's הוּ of כָמֹהוּ beside 'the like': folding it in is defensible, the unit note already names it, and rule 22 supports leaving the unrendered resumptive as its own unit. I did not move it, and I changed nothing to improve the agreement rate.
All three evidence requests were answered; nothing is left outstanding. Four conventions recorded and one amendment to rule 55 returned; no new rule.
